THE HOARD VAULT OF SORROWKEEP — knee-deep treasure fills a lightless stone chamber; foreground: tarnished crowns half-sunk in coin-drifts, scattered gemstones dulled by dust; midground: mountain of gold rising to vaulted ceiling carved with dragon-script, empty throne-dais sized for something immense; deep distance: tunnel exits show distant daylight, untouched for millennia; sky: through collapsed roof-section, winter stars gleam over wealth no living thing claims.

THE PETRIFIED EGG OF ASHENMOOR — single dragon egg large as a hay-cart rests on cracked pedestal; foreground: stone fragments from shell-cracks scattered in ritual circle, frost-rimed; midground: mineralized egg gleams with crystalline veins, shrine-pillars toppled around it; deep distance: ruined temple extends into fog, empty sanctum beyond; sky: heavy snowfall settling on the egg's fossilized surface, centuries accumulating in silence.

THE DRAGON-TEMPLE OF FORGOTTEN NAMES — mountain-carved cathedral with scaled architectural features; foreground: fallen column-capitals carved as dragon-claws, moss-covered; midground: vast entrance shaped as dragon-maw, stone teeth intact, interior darkness absolute; deep distance: processional stairs descend mountainside, pilgrim-statues headless and weathered; sky: storm clouds gather above the temple-peak where no prayers have risen for ages.

THE RIDER'S EYRIE — cliff-top outpost with crumbling dragon-perches; foreground: rusted saddle-hooks embedded in stone, leather straps rotted to threads; midground: semicircle of weathered standing-stones marking roost-positions, rune-carved; deep distance: valley far below where riders once patrolled, now empty farmland; sky: wind howls through the abandoned eyrie, carrying only the memory of wingbeats.

THE GLACIER WYRM — dragon skeleton locked in ice-face; foreground: single massive fang jutting from glacier, ice-blue and translucent; midground: entire serpentine form visible through ice, frozen mid-death, wings spread; deep distance: ice-field extends to horizon, burial-ground of the ancient cold; sky: aurora flickers over the glacial tomb, green light on frozen bone.

THE BATTLE-MURAL OF GREYSTONE PASS — canyon wall carved with war-scene relief; foreground: weathered chips of stone-carving scattered below, dragon-scale patterns; midground: cliff-face depicts dragon-combat spanning half-mile, details eroded by centuries of wind; deep distance: pass continues through mountains, carved memorial stretching beyond sight; sky: sunset casts long shadows across the relief, making dragons seem to move one final time.

THE SUNKEN HOARD OF MIREWOOD — treasure-filled chamber flooded by underground spring; foreground: gold coins shimmer beneath crystal-clear water, inches deep; midground: submerged throne and gem-heaps glow in shafts of light, vault perfectly preserved underwater; deep distance: flooded tunnels extend into darkness, treasury drowned and forgotten; sky: through collapsed ceiling, rain continues to fill the chamber, drop by endless drop.

THE CLUTCH-FLOOR OF EMBERHOLD — cave scattered with dragon eggshell fragments; foreground: petrified shell-shards the size of shields, inner membrane fossilized; midground: circular nest-depression carved in stone, seven egg-pedestals empty; deep distance: cavern depths show charred walls where hatchlings once breathed first flames; sky: through natural skylight, stars shine on the abandoned nursery of an extinct lineage.

THE VERTEBRAL BRIDGE — dragon spine spans a chasm; foreground: individual vertebrae fused into natural archway, bone smooth from centuries of wind; midground: entire spinal column bridges gorge, massive enough to walk across; deep distance: skeleton's tail disappears into rock-face, skull lost to time; sky: birds circle the bone-bridge, nesting in the hollow spaces where nerves once ran.

THE PROPHECY MOSAIC — throne-room floor depicting dragon-destinies; foreground: tesserae scattered where mosaic has crumbled, gold and lapis fragments; midground: floor-map shows dragon-territories in colored stone, spanning entire hall; deep distance: collapsed throne at chamber's end, meant for dragon-lord or rider-king; sky: through shattered dome, rain slowly erases the prophecies that never came to pass.

THE DRAGON-BONE CATHEDRAL — church built entirely from dragon skeletons; foreground: ribs form archways, individual bones carved with prayers; midground: skulls serve as altar-pieces, wings stretched as ceiling-vaults; deep distance: nave extends hundreds of feet, bone-architecture intact but empty; sky: through eye-socket windows, sunlight streams in sacred silence where hymns once echoed.

THE CLAW-MARKED PLATEAU — stone plain scarred by ancient dragon-landings; foreground: single talon-gouge deep as a trench, filled with rainwater; midground: plateau surface carved with hundreds of overlapping claw-marks, landing-patterns; deep distance: mountains ring the plateau, ancient dragon-gathering place; sky: clouds drift over the scarred stone, wind whistling through the grooves like phantom roars.

THE HOARD OF THOUSAND CROWNS — vault filled with royal regalia; foreground: scepters crossed on coin-piles, jewels scattered like gravel; midground: mountain of crowns from conquered kingdoms, tarnished gold rising to ceiling; deep distance: alcoves hold armor-sets sized for giants, tribute to dragon-overlord; sky: through crack in vault-roof, single beam of light illuminates dust motes above untouched wealth.

THE DRAGONRIDER MONUMENT — colossal statue of mounted warrior; foreground: fallen stone fragments carved with dedication-runes, vine-wrapped; midground: statue's base intact showing rider on dragon mid-flight, details eroded; deep distance: statue's upper half toppled across field, dragon-head shattered; sky: storm approaches the monument, lightning silhouetting what remains of forgotten glory.

THE FROST-EGG SHRINE — ice-cavern containing frozen dragon egg; foreground: ice-crystals form geometric patterns on egg-surface, pristine and cold; midground: egg suspended in ice-column, perfectly preserved, shrine-carved around it; deep distance: cavern depths show other empty pedestals, this clutch's sole survivor; sky: through ice-ceiling, pale arctic sun illuminates the frozen potential, never hatched.

THE PAINTED CAVE OF FIRST FLAME — underground gallery of dragon-art; foreground: pigment bowls still present, ochre and charcoal dried to dust; midground: cave walls covered in hand-painted dragons, primitive and reverent, colors fading; deep distance: tunnel system shows sequential murals depicting dragon-human first contact; sky: entrance far above shows daylight, paintings continuing into absolute darkness below.

THE WYRM-SKULL GATE — city entrance carved from dragon cranium; foreground: teeth individually carved as pillars, rune-inscribed; midground: entire skull embedded in city wall, eye-sockets serving as watchtowers; deep distance: abandoned city beyond gate, built to honor or appease; sky: ravens nest in skull-cavities, guardians of a dead civilization's threshold.

THE GOLDEN SLEEP CHAMBER — hoard arranged as dragon-bed; foreground: coins minted with forgotten dynasties, gem-facets catching light; midground: treasure sculpted into nest-shape, center-depression where dragon once coiled; deep distance: chamber walls show talon-polish from centuries of entry, tunnel leading to empty sky-exit; sky: through cave-mouth, sunset gilds the abandoned wealth, warm light on cold gold.

THE DRAGONSTONE CIRCLE — standing stones carved from shed dragon-scales; foreground: individual stone-scales large as shields, petrified and ancient; midground: circle of scale-stones surrounds central altar, each carved with dragon-name; deep distance: moorland extends to horizon, circle the only structure for miles; sky: storm-light plays across the petrified scales, once-living material now eternal monument.

THE EXCAVATION AT WYRMREST — archaeological dig uncovering dragon skeleton; foreground: brushes and tools abandoned beside exposed talon, work-in-progress; midground: partially unearthed skeleton emerging from hillside, grid-markers at each bone; deep distance: dig-camp deserted, tents empty, researchers fled or vanished; sky: evening descending on the half-revealed fossil, shadows filling excavation trenches.

THE MELTED THRONE ROOM — palace destroyed by dragon-fire; foreground: melted crown fused to stone, gold pooled and resolidified; midground: throne warped by impossible heat, walls glassed and crystallized; deep distance: entire hall shows fire-damage centuries old, aftermath frozen in time; sky: through melted roof-beams, stars shine on the testament to dragon-wrath, long cooled.

THE EGGSHELL MOUNTAIN — cliff-face embedded with fossilized dragon eggs; foreground: single cracked egg at path-level, interior hollow visible; midground: cliff shows dozens of eggs in stone, ancient nesting-site mineralized; deep distance: mountain continues upward, suggesting hundreds more eggs entombed in rock; sky: wind erodes the cliff grain by grain, slowly revealing the fossilized nursery to empty air.

THE LAST RIDER'S TOMB — memorial chamber for dragon and warrior; foreground: dragon-saddle on stone bier, leather cracked but recognizable; midground: parallel sarcophagi—human-sized and dragon-sized—both sealed with matching runes; deep distance: tomb-chapel carved with their deeds, companion-sculptures flanking entrance; sky: through tomb's single window, seasonal light marks centuries passing over the inseparable dead.

THE VALLEY OF THE COILED DEAD — dragon skeleton coiled cathedral-wide across a mist-filled valley floor, dead centuries; foreground scattered rib-fragments half-buried in black soil, tufts of grass threading bone; midground the full bleached coil, empty eye-sockets the size of millstones, skull resting in collapsed ruin of its own jaw; deep distance fog swallowing the tail-end entirely; sky cold pearl-grey, rooks circling the ridge above.

THE COIN-FLOOR VAULT — abandoned hoard-chamber beneath a collapsed mountain-fortress, knee-deep in tarnished gold; foreground loose coins, cracked gemstones, and a child-sized crown half-sunken in the drift; midground the main hoard-mound rising to the vaulted ceiling, crystallized dragon-spittle coating the walls in glassy amber sheets; deep distance the tunnel swallowing light entirely; sky absent, ceiling crack admitting one cold shaft of grey.

THE DRAGON WAR FRESCO — cathedral-nave mural stretching half a mile of crumbling plaster, depicting the great Dragon Wars; foreground chipped fresco-fragments littering the flagstones, a scholar's lantern casting orange across painted claws; midground the full mural parade of warring dragon-clans, ochre and dragon's-blood red, crazing with age; deep distance the nave dissolving into darkness where the last panel has collapsed entirely; sky visible through broken roof, ravens crossing.

THE SHRINE OF THE STONE EGG — single fossilized dragon egg the size of a carriage resting on a cracked stone pedestal in a collapsed open shrine; foreground moss-eaten offering bowls scattered at the pedestal base, dead votive candles centuries-cold; midground the egg itself, mineralized surface mapped with centuries of lichen, surface-cracks revealing grey stone core; deep distance shrine walls tumbled to vine-choked rubble; sky late amber through broken archways.

THE CLIFF-FACE EMBEDDED — dragon skeleton pinned vertical into a sea-cliff, preserved in the original death-pose, skull facing skyward; foreground wave-worn bone-chips on the shingle below, tide-wrack tangled around the lowest ribs; midground the full vertical skeleton spanning thirty meters of cliff-face, stained rust and white by salt and centuries; deep distance open grey sea merging with overcast; sky the colour of old pewter, gulls indifferent.

THE BONE-CATHEDRAL COLONNADE — temple-ruin built from actual dragon-bones lashed into column-arches, each rib a pillar; foreground fragments of fallen column-bone at the entrance, moss thick in the cracks; midground the colonnade receding inward, skull-lintels carved with runes, draped in vine curtains; deep distance the inner sanctum collapsed to rubble, a single altar visible through the green; sky filtered green-grey through canopy overhead.

THE ABANDONED EYRIE — cliff-top dragon-rider outpost, barracks walls crumbled to chest-height, roost-platforms rotten; foreground rusted chain-anchor rings embedded in the stone, wind-smoothed rune-markers, scraps of harness-leather; midground the main roost-deck overlooking an immense drop, saddle-stands empty, one still upright; deep distance the valley below lost in morning haze, the far mountains theoretical; sky wide and cold, wind-scored cloud streaming east.

THE OCHRE CAVE PAINTINGS — underground cave gallery, walls covered floor-to-ceiling in ochre dragon-paintings applied in dragon's-blood pigment; foreground a lone archaeologist's oil-lantern on the cave floor, scattered pigment-grinding stones; midground full gallery of dragons in flight, in council, in death, covering forty meters of cave wall; deep distance the tunnel narrowing to black beyond the final panel; sky absent, the cave absolute.

THE HOARD OF KINGS — vaulted underground chamber flooded knee-deep in gold, among it a ring of stolen crowns from devoured rulers; foreground individual crowns half-sunken in coins, one with a melted edge, one crushed by enormous weight; midground the full coin-sea glinting in torchlight, a throne-carved ledge for the absent occupant; deep distance the vault wall lost in dark beyond any torch's reach; sky absent, the chamber sealed for ages.

THE GLACIER CLUTCH — cluster of a dozen fossilized dragon eggs scattered across a cave floor at glacier's edge, most cracked open; foreground eggshell-fragments the size of paving stones, edges sharp where ancient hatching split them; midground the full clutch arranged in a rough nest-depression carved by claw-work, moss now filling the grooves; deep distance ice-wall sealing the cave's rear, blue and absolute; sky visible at the cave-mouth, overcast and distant.

THE MOUNTAIN-CUT CATHEDRAL — entire mountain-face carved into a dragon-cathedral, scaled-architecture detail still visible on surviving walls; foreground rubble-blocks bearing carved scale-relief at the entrance collapse-line; midground the vast carved interior, ceiling vaulted in stone-cut wing-motifs, half-collapsed; deep distance the inner nave fallen in, sky visible through the broken roof-crown; sky actual sky showing through the ruin, cold blue, empty.

THE MOSAIC FLOOR — underground hall, floor covered in a full-scale dragon-rider-last-stand mosaic in coloured stone, half-obscured by debris; foreground mosaic-tile fragments loose at the entry, the rider's hand visible in the cleared section; midground the full mosaic stretching twenty meters, dragon and rider against a stylized army, grout cracking, tiles missing in constellation-shapes; deep distance the hall wall bearing a commemorative inscription worn to near-illegibility; sky absent, torchlight only.

THE FALLEN RIDER MONUMENT — colossal stone statue of a dragon-rider and bound dragon, the rider-half toppled, the dragon-base still standing; foreground chunks of fallen rider-statue at the plinth base, face-fragment staring upward from the grass; midground the partial monument, dragon-base carved with memorial runes, rider-stump jagged against sky; deep distance a long processional avenue of smaller ruin-stones leading to it; sky bruised violet dusk, first stars appearing.

THE HALF-BURIED RIDGE SKELETON — dragon skeleton half-sunk into a ridgeline, emerging from earth as though diving, only dorsal spine and wingbones above ground; foreground loose vertebrae tumbled down the slope, rune-markers driven beside each exposed section; midground the great dorsal ridge rising four stories from the hillside, wingbone-arches framing the sky; deep distance the valley below mapped in autumn colour, tiny figures of two scholars at the base; sky wide grey with approaching rain.

THE CRYSTALLIZED LAIR — cavern-lair with walls coated in crystallized dragon-spittle, forming translucent amber stalactites over a bone-scattered floor; foreground jaw-bones and scattered claw-sheaths on the cave floor, a spilled hoard-coin here and there; midground the full cavern interior glowing faintly amber where light catches the crystallized walls; deep distance the lair-back lost in amber-dark; sky absent, one crack in the ceiling admitting a single white beam.

THE DROWNED TEMPLE RUIN — dragon-temple collapsed and partially flooded, columns of scaled architecture rising from black water; foreground stone-carved dragon-scale detail visible at the waterline, ripples spreading from no source; midground the temple floor underwater, gold visible through the murk, column-forest receding; deep distance the far wall still standing, mural-traces of a dragon procession above the waterline; sky reflected on the water surface, grey and rippled.

THE STANDING-STONE SHRINE — circle of standing stones each carved with a different dragon-clan rune, grass grown over the altar-stone; foreground lichen claiming the rune-carvings, a pilgrim's offering-stone wedged at the base of one monolith; midground the full stone circle standing in windswept moorland, each stone a different height; deep distance low hills rolling away under lead-sky; sky heavy overcast, the horizon the same grey as the stones.

THE PETRIFIED-FLAME HOARD — vast vault-chamber where the ceiling still bears petrified dragon-fire frozen mid-torrent in stone, above a deep hoard; foreground gold coins fused into clusters by ancient heat at the hoard's edge; midground the hoard-pile under petrified flame-ceiling, the stone torrent caught in impossible mid-pour above; deep distance the vault's rear wall a solid mass of melted-and-resolidified stone; sky absent, the petrified flame its own cold glow.

THE TREE-CRADLED EGG — single stone-hardened dragon egg the size of a cart cradled between the roots of an enormous ancient oak; foreground moss and root-hair wrapped around the lower curve, small wild-flowers at its base; midground the egg fully embraced by root-architecture, bark grown over one side as though the tree claimed it; deep distance old-growth forest receding in autumn haze; sky fragments of pale gold visible through canopy.

THE RIDER TOMB-MONUMENT — tomb-complex built for a dragon-rider and their named mount, twin sarcophagi in a half-collapsed mausoleum; foreground offering-fragments and withered garlands centuries-old at the tomb entrance; midground the twin sarcophagi side by side, the mount's depicted in carved-scale relief at twice human scale, both sealed, both silent; deep distance the mausoleum wall bearing a full carved account of their history; sky grey through the cracked dome overhead.

THE EMBEDDED CLIFF MURAL — natural cliff-face worked into a half-mile relief mural showing each of the seven dragon-clans in descending order; foreground fallen relief-chips in the scree below, a few still bearing painted detail; midground the cliff-face mural stretching in both directions beyond sight, scale-detail and clan-sigils intact in protected sections; deep distance the cliff curving away, the final clans lost to erosion and moss; sky evening red above the mesa-top.

THE BONE BRIDGE — dragon spine and ribcage repurposed as a bridge across a gorge, bones lashed with iron and mortared; foreground bone-surface worn smooth by centuries of foot-traffic, moss in the joint-gaps; midground the full bridge-arc of vertebral column spanning the gorge, ribs forming handrails; deep distance the gorge dropping to a white river far below, mist rising; sky pale winter blue above the far bank.

THE ICE-VAULT EGG — mineralized dragon egg embedded in the back wall of a glacier-vault, visible through two meters of clear ice; foreground explorers' chisel-marks at the ice-face, ice-chips on the cave floor, breath-fog visible; midground the egg behind the ice, dark grey stone veined with mineral colour, whole and sealed; deep distance the glacier-cave narrowing to impassable blue; sky at the cave-mouth far behind, white overcast.

THE SUNKEN HOARD-THRONE — underground vault with a throne carved to seat something the size of a war-elephant, surrounded by hoard-tide; foreground individual artefacts at the hoard-edge: a sceptre, a shattered war-helm, a bishop's crook half-swallowed by coins; midground the throne itself rising from gold, scaled stone armrests worn smooth, empty; deep distance the vault ceiling lost in dark above the hoard-peak; sky absent, a single wall-torch long-dead its only marker.

THE VALLEY-SPANNING SKELETON — dragon-skeleton category A; foreground scattered vertebrae the size of mill-wheels half-buried in river-mud, each joint marked by rune-carved survey stakes planted by long-dead scholars; midground the full ribcage arching cathedral-high across the valley floor, bleached white and picked utterly clean, empty sockets facing skyward in the original death-pose, vines threading through every rib; deep distance the skull alone fills the far cliff-face, wedged between granite walls like something the mountain swallowed; sky grey overcast bleeding thin light down the length of bones that stretch half a mile end to end.

THE HOARD VAULT OF CROWNS — dragon-lair category C; foreground knee-deep gold coins lapping against the shins of a single robed archivist barely visible in the chamber's near edge, scattered among the coins the crushed circlets of a dozen devoured kings; midground a vaulted cavern whose ceiling is scorched black by ancient fire, crystallized dragon-spittle hanging from the roof like amber chandeliers, the hoard so deep entire suits of armor protrude only as gauntlets and helms above the gold; deep distance iron vault-doors stand open and warped outward as though something very large once shouldered through; sky none — the vault is sealed, lantern-light only, suffocating and golden.

THE DRAGON-WARS CATHEDRAL FRESCO — mural category B; foreground flakes of painted plaster littering the floor in drifts like autumn leaves, each fragment showing a scale, a wing-edge, a rider's gauntlet; midground the west wall of the ruined cathedral stretching sixty feet high, the fresco intact across two-thirds of it depicting ranked dragon-clans arrayed in battle above burning cities, the colors still vivid in ochre and dragon's-blood red; deep distance the collapsed east wall has let in a century of weather, and the fresco there is blank grey wash; sky open to rafterless ruin, ravens circling the clerestory gap.

THE CLUTCH FLOOR — fossilized egg category D; foreground shards of mineralized eggshell thick as roof-tiles scattered across a sand floor, some pieces still curved and showing faint scale-impressions on their interior surface; midground a broad depression in the cavern floor ringed by heat-cracked stone where a full clutch once lay, three intact fossilized eggs remaining, each the size of a cartwright's wagon, their surfaces gone to grey stone and quartz veining; deep distance the cavern throat recedes into darkness, the walls scorched in great circular sweeps by what must once have been a brooding flame; sky none — deep underground, torch-shadows only.

THE GLACIER-BURIED WYRM — skeleton category A; foreground ice chips and meltwater pooling around the excavation trench, scattered with small hand-tools and measurement cords left by scholars who did not return; midground the dragon-skeleton visible through translucent blue-white glacier ice as a dark armature, the spine running a full two hundred feet before vanishing deeper into the ice-face, every bone held suspended in perfect original articulation; deep distance the glacier calves into a mountain lake, the far shore lost in freezing mist; sky iron-pale winter light refracting through the ice-face, turning the buried bones faintly violet.

THE SCALED-ARCH TEMPLE — dragon-temple category E; foreground cracked flagstones between which pale grass forces upward, scattered with offerings of corroded bronze bowls and antler-handled knives left by the last worshippers centuries past; midground a colonnade of pillars each carved as a coiled dragon-body, the scales rendered in obsidian inlay now mostly pried out by scavengers, the colonnade roof long collapsed between every third span; deep distance the inner sanctum's dome has fallen in, rubble mounded at the altar's base, but the altar-stone itself remains — a single granite slab carved with a dragon-wing spread wide enough to land upon; sky afternoon sun splitting through the fallen dome-hole in a single column of dusty light.

THE RIDER'S TOMB-MONUMENT — dragon-rider category F; foreground weather-smoothed offerings at the monument's plinth — corroded coins, a crumbled wreath, a child's carved wooden dragon worn to near-featurelessness; midground a twin statue, rider and mount, the mount twice the size of the rider and both rendered in granite now furred with grey-green lichen, the rider's features entirely eroded away, the dragon-mount's skull cracked along the jaw by a frost-heave so old trees have rooted in the gap; deep distance an eyrie platform behind the monument, the iron tie-rings for dragon-harness still visible, the cliff-drop beyond absolute; sky high cirrus cloud, the monument catching wind that makes no sound it was built to catch.

THE HALF-MILE CAVE MURAL — mural category B; foreground the cavern entrance where pigment-dusted handprints in ochre and charcoal edge the arch, left by the painters themselves as signatures, now faded to whispers; midground the mural running the full length of the cave passage — each dragon clan given its own panel in dragon's-blood red and manganese black, riders shown as tiny figures beside mounts whose wings span floor to ceiling; deep distance the mural wraps the terminal chamber in a continuous panorama of the last great convening before the silence fell, unwitnessed now except by cave-beetles and dark; sky none — the cave curves underground, oil-lamp black.

THE COIN-FLOODED THRONE CHAMBER — hoard category C; foreground a scholar's wading-boots visible above the gold-coin surface, the figure itself waist-deep and barely present, a measuring-rod extended to gauge the depth; midground a throne carved directly from bedrock scaled up for a creature twenty times human size, the armrests worn smooth by centuries of a vast weight resting there, the seat filled now with settled gold; deep distance the chamber's far wall bears a fire-damage pattern in concentric black rings where a dragon once exhaled greeting or rage, the pattern spreading thirty feet; sky a shaft in the vault ceiling opens to sky, and a single rope descends — the scholars' only exit.

THE PETRIFIED EGG SHRINE — egg category D; foreground votive candles long melted to pale wax puddles on the shrine steps, their wicks blackened, a few copper pins thrust into the cracks between stones as old prayers; midground a single fossilized dragon-egg on a stone pedestal of obvious antiquity, the egg itself the size of a carriage, its surface veined through with white quartz and iron-oxide rust, cradled by iron arms forged to fit its exact curve; deep distance the shrine walls are covered in prayer-inscriptions in three dead scripts, the earliest layer nearly worn smooth, the latest layer still just legible; sky a single oculus above the egg, the light having tracked across it every day for four hundred years, bleaching the pedestal top pale.

THE CLIFF-FACE PINNED SKELETON — skeleton category A; foreground a rope-ladder hanging from the nearest rib, two archaeologists the size of sparrows at this scale clinging halfway up, their presence making the scale undeniable; midground the full dragon-skeleton pressed flat against a granite cliff-face as though it fell there and the stone held it — the wingspan spread two hundred feet across the rock, bones bleached by exposure, the skull forward and down as if looking at the valley it once owned; deep distance the valley below is forest-reclaimed, no road, no village, the trees grown up around bones that fell before anyone now living was born; sky low cloud wrapping the cliff-top, the uppermost wing-tip bones disappearing into mist.

THE ABANDONED EYRIE BARRACKS — dragon-rider category F; foreground rotted leather harness-straps still looped through iron wall-rings, the leather crumbled to dark powder at a touch, beside them a wooden chest whose lid has fallen inward, spilling corroded buckles and a single intact flight-glove still shaped to a fist; midground a long stone hall built into the cliff-edge, the seaward wall entirely open to the drop, roost-perches of iron scaffolding extending over the void for dragons to land upon, four of the six perches broken and fallen; deep distance the cliff drops to a grey sea a thousand feet below, and across the water the ruins of a signal-tower on a sea-stack still stands, its fire-bowl gone dark a century ago; sky storm light, the wind at this altitude a constant low howl through every open wall.

THE DRAGON-BONE BRIDGE — skeleton category A; foreground the bridge's nearside abutment where a scholar's survey parchment is pinned to a stake, fluttering in the gorge-wind, the ink-lines mapping bone-segments of the original anatomy; midground two massive dragon-femurs lashed with ancient ironwork form the bridge's primary span across a mountain gorge, the bones scraped smooth by a thousand years of foot-traffic, yellow-white and utterly structural, load-bearing what no stone arch attempted; deep distance the far bank where the bridge meets the gorge wall, carved handholds worn smooth by generations who crossed without understanding what they walked on; sky the gorge itself acts as a wind-funnel, cloud streaming through at bridge-level like the dragon's last breath still moving.

THE HOARD WITH PETRIFIED FLAME — hoard category C; foreground scattered gems half-swallowed by a calcified crust covering the chamber floor, the crust cracked in places where the weight of gold above eventually pressed through; midground a column of petrified fire — the actual moment of a dragon's breath caught in stone, rising from a floor-vent and frozen mid-gout, the orange-amber translucent stone lit internally by a faint bioluminescent fungus that has colonized its cracks; deep distance the hoard banks against every wall to shoulder-height, a tide of centuries-settled gold, and at its center the petrified flame stands like a monument to the moment everything ended; sky none — the vault ceiling is intact, the only light the eerie amber glow of the fossil-fire.

THE MOSAIC FLOOR OF THE LAST STAND — mural category B; foreground a tarp pulled back by excavators weighted at the corners with fist-sized stones, the mosaic beneath still wet from recent clearing, tesserae glinting under raking lantern-light; midground the mosaic filling the entire floor of a collapsed hall — a dragon-rider's last stand depicted in extraordinary tesserae detail, the rider shown at the mosaic's center ringed by enemies, the dragon-mount's shadow cast behind the rider larger than anything else in the image, a presence defined by outline alone; deep distance the hall's far wall has collapsed inward and the mosaic there is rubble, the story's ending buried under its own structure; sky the excavation is open-air now that the roof is gone, overcast afternoon, rain-threat hanging.

THE MOUNTAIN-CUT DRAGON CATHEDRAL — dragon-temple category E; foreground approach steps carved from the mountain itself, each riser so tall a human must step up with both hands, designed for a congregation that did not walk on two legs; midground the cathedral interior cut entirely from living rock, the ceiling vaulted in exact imitation of a dragon's ribcage — each stone rib positioned anatomically — and the nave wide enough that a fully-spread pair of wings would barely touch the walls; deep distance the altar end carved with a single massive dragon-face emerging from the rock, its mouth open as if in song or decree, the interior of the mouth a fire-channel blackened by sacred flame now long cold; sky the cathedral has no windows — only a single oculus in the vault through which rain has been falling for four hundred years, pooling on the altar-stone.

THE HOARD OF KING-BONES — Dragon hoard in a collapsed vault where the gold half-buries skeletal human remains — the eaten — not the dragon; foreground finger-bones visible in coin-drifts, a crown still on a skull half-sunk in gold; midground the full vault-floor, the sheer quantity of human dead suggesting centuries of tribute and violence, the gold indifferent to what it cost; deep distance the vault ceiling partially collapsed, starlight visible through a single crack above; sky glimpsed through rubble — cold stars, no moon.

THE HALF-FALLEN RIDER COLOSSUS — A colossal stone statue of a dragon-rider, the mount-half collapsed, the rider-half still standing; foreground massive stone dragon-wing fragments scattered around the base, the texture of carved scales still detailed on every shard; midground the rider-figure, thirty feet high from plinth to helm, one arm extended in command, the dragon it once rode collapsed beneath it into rubble; deep distance a road leading away from the monument, overgrown, the civilization that built this long finished; sky afternoon grey, rooks circling the statue's outstretched arm.

THE RUNE-MARKED SKELETON EXCAVATION — Dragon skeleton partially excavated across a valley floor, rune-markers at every joint driven by a long-dead scholarly expedition; foreground the nearest joint-marker, a bronze spike with carved notation, green with age, the bone it marks a vertebra the size of a millstone; midground the excavation as a whole — nearly forty markers stretching the valley's length, the skeleton's full outline comprehensible from this, cathedral-vast; deep distance the valley's far end where the skull rests, still half-buried; sky low cloud, a persistent grey drizzle softening everything.

THE VAULT OF FALLEN KINGS — abandoned dragon hoard; foreground knee-deep scatter of tarnished crowns, split goblets, and finger-bones of long-dead treasury-guards pressed flat beneath coin-weight; midground vaulted cavern whose ceiling arches cathedral-high, gold drifts banked against carved stone walls, a throne the size of a watchtower chiseled from basalt to cradle a dragon's haunches; deep distance the far wall lost in amber haze where centuries of accumulated coin-dust suspends in still air; sky the vault mouth above sealed by collapsed stone, a single ceiling-crack admitting one pale column of daylight that illuminates nothing but more gold.

THE CLIFF-FACE COLOSSAL — dragon skeleton embedded in sandstone escarpment; foreground chipped rune-markers driven at each exposed joint by long-dead scholars, their parchment flags rotted to tatters fluttering on iron pins; midground the skeleton itself spans three hundred feet of cliff, ribs curving outward like the arches of a drowned cathedral, the skull half-freed from rock with empty eye-sockets the diameter of mill-wheels; deep distance the valley below the cliff floored with centuries of shed sandstone fragments, each fragment bearing partial bone-impression; sky high pale overcast pressing colorless light against bone that has not moved in a thousand years.

THE HOARD OF CRYSTALLIZED BREATH — vaulted cavern with petrified dragon-flame; foreground thumbnail-sized shards of vitrified stone scattered across the entry passage, each shard refracting torchlight like amber; midground the main chamber where a single sustained exhalation of dragonfire centuries ago has crystallized mid-air into a translucent amber mass the size of a merchant-ship frozen in the act of erupting from the far wall, coins and melted weaponry entombed inside it; deep distance the hoard-piles behind the crystallized flame still half-visible through amber, a fortune sealed in geological time; sky the cavern dome above the frozen fire, scorched to glass, reflecting the amber mass below in a distorted ceiling-mirror.

THE DRAGON-TEMPLE COLONNADE — crumbling temple built to dragons with scaled stone architecture; foreground fallen column drums on the approach road, each drum carved with overlapping scale-pattern, moss thickening in every carved groove; midground the colonnade itself still standing in fragments, alternating columns upright and toppled, each column capital carved as a coiled dragon-tail, the proportions of the whole structure suggesting the interior was never meant for human standing-height; deep distance the temple cella behind the colonnade, its roof long collapsed inward, a heap of scaled-stone rubble filling the nave to half its original height; sky the temple faces east, receiving flat morning light that throws the scale-carving into sharp relief and fills the shadows with cold blue.

THE SHRINE EGG — single fossilized dragon-egg on a stone pedestal in a collapsed shrine; foreground scattered votive offerings around the pedestal base: corroded copper coins, crumbled flower-impressions pressed into old wax, a child's carved wooden dragon worn to near-formlessness; midground the egg itself the size of a carriage, its surface mineralized over centuries to striated grey-green stone though the original shell-texture survives in every scale-facet across its girth, seated on a pedestal carved with supplicant-figures no taller than the egg's equator; deep distance the shrine walls leaning inward under roof-collapse, the ceiling a tangle of fallen timber and vine, the egg outlasting all architecture built to honor it; sky visible only as a ragged rectangle of overcast through the collapse-hole in the roof directly above the pedestal.

THE ABANDONMENT VAULT — coin-flooded dragon hoard chamber with a throne for no one; foreground coin-sediment layered to knee-depth across the entire floor, the uppermost layer oxidized green, lower layers visible in cross-section where explorers have waded a path through the middle of the room; midground the throne carved directly from the living rock at the chamber's far end, its seat the width of a barn-floor, its armrests shaped as dragon-forelimbs, the throne surface smooth from use then coated in a century of undisturbed dust; deep distance the hoard-piles rising against every wall above the coin-flood, crowns stacked on crowns, scepters jutting from the mass like reeds, all of it in the dark beyond the explorers' torchlight-reach; sky the ceiling above the throne carved in relief-work showing a dragon descending in blessing toward whoever sat below, the stone wings spanning the full vault-width.

THE PETRIFIED NEST — cluster of cracked dragon-eggshells across a clutch-floor; foreground eggshell fragments the size of paving-stones scattered for thirty feet in every direction from the nest-center, their inner surfaces smooth and pale, their outer surfaces mineralized to rough grey-brown; midground the clutch-depression itself, a shallow bowl of compressed earth and ancient charcoal-ash forty feet across, the shells arranged in the ghost-pattern of six original eggs now all broken open from within though nothing living emerged long enough to leave more than scratches in the ash; deep distance the cave walls flanking the clutch-floor scorched black at a height suggesting the brooding dragon's body-heat radiated outward at wing-height; sky the cave ceiling above the nest stained in concentric heat-rings, darkest at center, fading to unburned rock at the edges.

THE RIDGE-SPINE FOSSIL — dragon spine embedded in a mountain ridge; foreground loose shale on the trail up to the ridge, each flat slab imprinted with scale-fossil where it has cleaved along the original burial-plane; midground the ridge itself revealing, upon approach, that its entire crest is a single unbroken dorsal-spine column — vertebrae fused by millennia of geological pressure into what reads at distance as a natural ridge-line, only the repeating knob-pattern of articulated bone betraying its origin; deep distance the ridge running for two miles to the next peak, the spine never deviating, the mountain range built partly around what it contains; sky clear altitude-blue above the ridge-crest, the spine casting a toothed shadow-line down the southern slope in the afternoon sun.

THE SUNKEN HOARD HALL — flooded dragon-vault with treasure visible through black water; foreground the submerged entry stair, water beginning at the third step down, the lower steps furred with pale algae, scattered gold coins on the dry steps above the waterline placed there by centuries of ebb-and-flow; midground the vault itself flooded to ceiling-level, the treasure-mass below the water visible as a shifting golden floor eight feet down, crowns and chalices and weapon-hilts rising from the hoard-floor toward the surface like a drowned city seen from above; deep distance the far end of the flooded vault in total darkness beneath the water, the hoard continuing beyond visibility; sky the vault entrance admits exterior light that falls across the water-surface and refracts downward in shifting pale columns onto gold.

THE DRAGON-CATHEDRAL MOUNTAIN-CUT — temple carved into a mountain face for dragon-scale worship; foreground the processional approach road of flagstones each carved with a single scale-symbol, centuries of pilgrim-feet having worn the symbols to shallow depressions; midground the facade itself cut directly into the mountain cliff-face, the entrance arch thirty feet high and forty feet wide framing absolute interior darkness, the arch carved with dragon-anatomy in cross-section — a scholarly dissection-diagram rendered in devotional stone; deep distance the interior visible only as a suggestion of vaulted space beyond the entrance, the far wall too distant for the outside light to reach; sky the mountain face above the temple-entrance carved with a relief of the dragon-god for which the temple was built, the relief spanning a hundred feet of cliff, the face worn by weather to a suggestion of majesty.

THE RELIQUARY CLAW — single dragon claw mounted on a stone altar in a ruined shrine; foreground dried flower-offerings crumbled to brown dust across the altar-base, accumulated over generations of visitors, the most recent decades-old; midground the claw itself the size of a longsword, its keratin surface fossilized to translucent amber-yellow, mounted in iron brackets on a stone plinth carved with protective runes, a crack running through the claw's middle-third from some long-ago impact but the two halves held together by the brackets; deep distance the shrine-room around the altar, its walls painted with supplicant-figures each bearing smaller dragon-relics now absent, the painted offerings visible where the actual objects were removed; sky the shrine's oculus above the altar open to sky, rain having discolored the altar-stone in a spreading stain outward from center.

THE DRAGON-SCALE STANDING STONES — standing-stone shrine carved with dragon-runes in a moorland ring; foreground peat and heather growing to the base of each stone, the lower carved faces half-buried by centuries of slow peat-accumulation; midground the stone ring itself, nine monoliths each fifteen feet tall, their faces carved on all four sides with the same script in repeating variations — a dragon-naming liturgy according to the scholars who have attempted translation — the stones leaning at various degrees of ancient settlement; deep distance the moorland stretching away from the ring in all directions, featureless and brown, the stones visible for miles as the only vertical interruption; sky heavy moorland overcast, the light flat and directionless, the rune-shadows indistinct, the stones needing raking light to be read and receiving none.

THE FROZEN CLUTCH — fossilized dragon-egg embedded in alpine ice, visible from a pass; foreground the icy surface of the glacier at the pass-level, a field of wind-scoured blue-white ice, crampons-marks from previous scholars still faintly pressed into the surface; midground the egg visible two feet below the ice-surface, its scale-pattern perfectly preserved by the freezing, its color a deep red-brown seen through ice-filter as burgundy, its size requiring the viewer to stand back thirty feet to see the full ovoid — as large as a merchant's wagon; deep distance the glacier continuing downslope, the egg's burial site unremarkable within the field of ice, the scale only apparent with the midground pass-road as reference; sky clear alpine blue above the pass, the sun at the angle where it penetrates the ice surface and illuminates the egg from above as though staged.

THE WEATHERED CLAW MARKS — cliff-face claw-gouges where a dragon landed for centuries; foreground loose stone chips at the cliff-base, each chip bearing a partial groove-scar from the same geological event, accumulated over the centuries from freeze-thaw expansion of the claw-cuts above; midground the cliff-face itself at the base of a natural platform, four parallel gouges cut into the stone at a height of twelve feet from the ground and extending upward for thirty feet, each gouge the width of a man's torso, the repeated use having worn the stone surface between cuts smooth and slightly concave where chest-scales would have rested; deep distance the platform above the gouged cliff-face, its stone surface dark and polished from the same repeated landings, a fire-scorched area at the platform's center where prey was consumed; sky the cliff-platform sky-facing, open in the direction the dragon would have launched, a wide unobstructed view that explains the preference.

THE BONE-VAULT CEILING — dragon skeleton coiled across the ceiling of a buried vault, pinned there by its own death-pose; foreground the vault floor littered with small bones that fell from the ceiling over centuries, each one tagged by a previous expedition with a numbered iron pin; midground looking upward at the skeleton itself mapped across thirty feet of ceiling like a grotesque chandelier, the ribs hanging downward like the vaulting of an inverted cathedral, the skull at the ceiling's center with empty sockets facing the floor, the entire skeleton held in place by the collapse of stone around it at the moment of death, the rock having sealed around the body before decomposition could disarticulate it; deep distance the vault's far corners in shadow where the bones thin out to tail-tip, the last vertebrae disappearing into the wall-stone; sky the vault-ceiling is the sky of this space, forty feet overhead, covered entirely in bleached bone and ancient stone, no opening, no light except what the explorers carry.

[THE VAULT OF FALLEN CROWNS] — abandoned dragon-hoard vaulted beneath a collapsed keep; foreground knee-deep scatter of tarnished coins, fractured scepters, and king's crowns with gemstones missing, pried loose by centuries of frost; midground the vast low-ceilinged chamber stretching cathedral-wide, gold mounded in drifts shoulder-high against walls scorched black by ancient heat; deep distance a second archway leading into total darkness where the hoard continues unmeasured; sky a single crack in the vaulted roof admitting one pale shaft of dust-thick light onto untouched gold.

[THE CLUTCH-FLOOR OF ASHENMERE] — fossilized dragon-egg cluster strewn across a collapsed underground shrine; foreground cracked eggshell fragments the thickness of roof-slates, edges mineralized grey-white, scattered among drifted sand and old nesting-ash; midground seven fossilized eggs the size of carthorses arranged in a rough circle, each cracked open from within centuries ago, the broken halves sunken and overgrown by pale cave-moss; deep distance the shrine walls carved with hatching-rites in angular runes now illegible under calcite bloom; sky the vaulted ceiling above dense with stalactites grown slow over the long unvisited dark.
